fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Reconfigurable organisms built from Xenopus cells maintain their externally imposed shape and also self-repair after damage, for example automatically closing lacerations.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Finally, reconfigurable organisms not only self-maintain their externally imposed configuration, but they also self-repair in the face of damage, such as automatically closing lacerations (SI Appendix, Fig. S9).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Discussion”. Scope: Xenopus laevis reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Laceration closure is a direct image-derived endpoint. Existing supplementary evidence can verify examples but does not appear broad enough to establish general self-repair or cleanly separate active healing from passive mechanics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure wound area and external-shape deviation over time after laceration, comparing closure and shape maintenance with dead-tissue or mechanically passive controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Few injury cases and incomplete raw time series limit estimates of reliability.

Simple elastic closure must be distinguished from active repair.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.95
data existence: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Wound closure and shape maintenance are measurable. The published support is an illustrative supplementary figure, and re-inspecting that figure is not a test of rates, sample size, or passive recoil. A quantitative decision needs the original time series or a new assay.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After a standardized laceration, measure wound width over time against uninjured shape landmarks; self-repair holds if the gap closes and the external configuration returns, beyond passive recoil.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The support is a supplementary example, not a deposited series with sample size and controls.

Tissue recoil and wound contraction can close a gap without a regulated repair response.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.45
data existence: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.25
